spans.s:
n. (-तं)
A drug, a medicament.
E.
भिषज् a physician, and जित subdued, (by whom.)

m. (-षक्)
A Vaidya or physician.
E.
भी to fear, अजि Uṇādi aff., and षुक् augment; or भिषज् a Kaṇḍvādi root, to overcome, (disease,) aff. क्विप्.

f. (-टा)
Scorched rice.
E.
भिस्सा boiled rice, टीक to go or resemble, ड aff.; this word is variously read भिस्सिटा, भिष्मिटा, भिष्मिष्टा, भिष्मिका.

f. (-स्सा)
Boiled rice.
E.
भिट् to break, aff. क्विप्, षो to destroy, aff. क, and the द of भिट् changed irr. to स; also read भिष्माः see the last.

f. (-षा)
Terrifying, frightening, intimidation.
E.
भी to fear, causal v., अङ् and टाप् affs.

mfn. (-णः-णा-णं)
1 Horrible, terrific, formidable.
2 Hard, harsh.
3 Exciting the sentiment of horror, applied to poetical compositions.
m. (-णः)
The olibanum tree, (Boswellia thurifera.)
2 A name of ŚIVA.
n. (-णं)
1 Horror, terror, the property that excites fear.
2 The sentiment of horror as the object of poetical composition.
E.
भी to fear, in the causal form, aff. ल्युट् or युच्.

mfn. (-णः-णा-णं)
Terrifying, frightening.
E.
भी to fear, causal v., शानच् aff.

mfn. (-ष्मः-ष्मा-ष्मं)
Horrible, terrific, fearful.
n. (-ष्मं)
Horror, horribleness, the property of exciting fear or terror.
m. (-ष्मः)
1 A name of Ś

An imp, a goblin.
E.
भी to fear, मक् Uṇādi aff. and षुक् augment.

f. (-सूः)
The Ganges.
E.
भीष्म the prince so named, and सू mother, being the mother of BHĪṢMA by ŚĀNTANU.
